question.problem:
Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $3x+6y=18?$

I. $(10,-1)$

II. $(4,1)$

III. $(-6,6)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(10,-1)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=10$ and $y=-1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+6y & =18 \\ 3\cdot 10+6\cdot (-1) & =18 \\ 30-6 & =18 \\ 24 & \ne 18\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(4,1)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=4$ and $y=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+6y & =18 \\ 3\cdot 4+6\cdot 1 & =18 \\ 12+6 & =18 \\ 18 & =18\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(-6,6)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=-6$ and $y=6,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+6y & =18 \\ 3\cdot (-6)+6\cdot 6 & =18 \\ -18+36 & =18 \\ 18 & =18\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
